events.title: Hispanic Heritage Month 2026
events.description:
Hispanic Heritage Month 2026
“Unidos Somos Más — Together We Are More!”

Join the Stony Brook University community as we celebrate 37 years of Hispanic Heritage Month at SBU!

From September 15 through November 6, we invite students, faculty, staff, departments, student organizations, and community partners to celebrate the rich cultures, histories, identities, achievements, and contributions of Latine communities.

This year’s theme, “Unidos Somos Más — Together We Are More!”, reflects the strength and possibilities that emerge when we come together, share our stories, celebrate our wide range of identities, and build meaningful connections. The Hispanic Heritage Month Committee, DICE, and campus partners will offer a variety of cultural, educational, social, and community-building programs for the Stony Brook community.

Whether you are a department, student organization, faculty or staff member, or community partner, we invite you to take part in HHM 2026. Attend a signature event, support a student organization, learn something new, share your culture, or host an event or initiative of your own. Every contribution helps make Hispanic Heritage Month a more vibrant and inclusive reflection of our community.

Whether through the arts, music and food, cultural traditions, meaningful dialogue, educational programs, academic/research opportunities, career networking, awards and scholarships, civic engagement, or simply connecting, there are many ways to celebrate, participate, and be part of HHM. 

For event details and the full Hispanic Heritage Month 2026 calendar, visit www.stonybrook.edu/hhm.

Because when we come together, Unidos Somos Más — Together We Are More!

events.title: SBUHacks
events.description:
SBUHacks is Stony Brook University's 36-hour hackathon, hosted by the Computing Society at Stony Brook. Over one nonstop weekend, students of every skill level team up to design, build, and demo a project from scratch. Whether it's a web app, a hardware hack, a game, or an AI experiment, the only limits are your imagination and the clock. Throughout the event you'll find workshops led by mentors and industry sponsors, opportunities to network with recruiters, and plenty of food, swag, and late-night fun to keep the energy up. At the end of the 36 hours, teams present their creations to a panel of judges for prizes across multiple tracks. Beginners are welcome and encouraged; no prior hackathon experience is needed. Come learn something new, meet fellow builders, and ship something you're proud of.

events.title: To God’s Ear: A Film Screening
events.description:
Filmed on the North Fork of Long Island, To God’s Ear is an independent film by veteran director and writer Stan Schofield about trauma, grief, resilience, and the healing power of connection.

The film follows the unlikely friendship between two teenage girls who face trauma and loss as they learn to trust one another and find healing through their bond with a special horse. Their journey brings together two grieving families searching for hope and redemption as they explore the unique bond between humans and horses and the potential of equine therapy to support healing.

Free for students, faculty, and staff. Click link to register: https://forms.gle/rPw1drS5z3HkxrHEA

events.title: University Affairs Committee Meeting
events.description:
The University Affairs Committee serves as a space for undergraduate students to raise concerns, discuss campus-wide issues, and work on initiatives that improve the student experience at Stony Brook University. Led by the Vice President of University Affairs, the committee focuses on areas such as academic policies, accessibility, transportation and parking, campus technology, student services, and other university-wide concerns.

Committee members work together to gather student feedback, develop advocacy initiatives, research potential policy solutions, and communicate student concerns to university administrators and shared governance bodies. The committee also helps strengthen undergraduate representation within University governance and provides students with an opportunity to become directly involved in creating positive change on campus.

All undergraduate students are welcome to attend, share concerns, propose ideas, and get involved in University Affairs initiatives.

events.title: Relating Majors to Minors w/ The Career Center!
events.description:
Myth: A student's major ties them to a specific career path. 
Truth: While some majors help students develop specialized skills, most people end up working in careers that are not directly related to their major. 

What employers really value are the career-life skills that can be developed through a variety of majors. This module focuses on how to connect majors of interest to possible career paths. We explore strategies for deciding on a major and tools to identify related careers.

Join us learn the following:

Describe the relationship between majors and careers
Identify three strategies for exploring majors and careers of interest
Develop a plan to explore a career area of interest

events.title: NMDP x SBU Biweekly Tabling
events.description:
NMDP x SBU is the stony brook chapter of NMDP, an international non-profit dedicated to supporting blood stem cell donation. Blood stem cell donation is a curative treatment for blood disorders including but not limited to leukemia, lymphoma and sickle cell anemia. The limitation to blood stem cell donation is that the donor and recipient must be a genetic match to ensure the patient's body does not reject the donation. Due to wide genetic diversity, it is extremely difficult for searching patients to find a genetic match, but with every new member of the registry, a patient's chance increases. Our tabling is focused on both education and recruitment for the stony brook university community!

events.title: USG Club Co-Lab: Community Awareness and Service Organizations
events.description:
USG x SEA Club Co-Lab Series

USG and Student Engagement & Activities invite club leaders to the Club Co-Lab Series, a set of collaborative working sessions organized by club category. Each Co-Lab is designed to help organizations meet relevant partners, share resources, develop joint-event ideas, and leave with practical next steps for collaboration.

Each session will include networking, an icebreaker, a brief USG presentation on funding, treasury information, the Club Closet, and important SEA guidelines, followed by a department-specific resource presentation and interactive collaboration activities. Clubs will take part in activities such as Resources Bingo, scenario planning, and a “Build Your Own Event” challenge that helps them identify potential partners and turn an idea into a feasible program.

USG will also collect feedback and follow up on collaboration commitments so that these conversations lead to real partnerships, shared programming, and stronger support for clubs throughout the year. Attendees will have the opportunity to win snacks and gift-card incentives.

We strongly encourage each organization to send at least two representatives, ideally members of the club’s Core Four: President, Vice President, Secretary, and Treasurer.

Club Co-Lab Schedule

September 14: Sports Clubs
September 16: Academic and Honor Societies
September 28: Cultural Organizations
September 30: Activism and Advocacy Organizations
October 19: Religious and Spiritual Organizations
October 21: Leisure Activities Organizations
October 28: Community Awareness and Service Organizations
November 4: Performance Clubs

Unless otherwise indicated on the individual event page, sessions will be held in Student Activities Center (SAC) 302. Please attend the session that best fits your organization’s primary category.

Acclaimed Stony Brook Music faculty members Jennifer Frautschi, violin, and Christina Dahl, piano, perform a program of musical rarities: two 19th-century gems paired with two rare 20th-century voices. They begin the program with Beethoven’s Violin Sonata No. 4 and end the program with Saint-Saëns Violin Sonata No. 1. In between, travel on a musical journey from Elgar's nostalgic warmth to the virtuosity and intensity of Schoenberg's rhapsodic Phantasy. 

Program:
Beethoven Violin Sonata No. 4 in A minor, Op. 23
Elgar Violin Sonata in E minor, Op. 82
Schoenberg Phantasy for Violin with Piano Accompaniment, Op. 47
Saint-Saëns Violin Sonata No. 1 in D minor, Op. 75

events.description:
Delta Sigma Pi will be hosting a DIY Bird Feeder Crafting Event focused on environmental awareness and wildlife conservation. The event will begin with a brief presentation discussing environmental issues and their impact on local wildlife, particularly birds and their habitats. Following the presentation, participants will create bird feeders using pine cones, birdseed, animal-friendly peanut butter, and string.

This hands-on activity aims to encourage environmental responsibility, creativity, and community engagement while educating participants on simple ways to support local wildlife. Participants will be able to take their completed bird feeders home and hang them in suitable outdoor spaces to help provide food for birds.

events.title: University Affairs Committee Meeting
events.description:
The University Affairs Committee serves as a space for undergraduate students to raise concerns, discuss campus-wide issues, and work on initiatives that improve the student experience at Stony Brook University. Led by the Vice President of University Affairs, the committee focuses on areas such as academic policies, accessibility, transportation and parking, campus technology, student services, and other university-wide concerns.

Committee members work together to gather student feedback, develop advocacy initiatives, research potential policy solutions, and communicate student concerns to university administrators and shared governance bodies. The committee also helps strengthen undergraduate representation within University governance and provides students with an opportunity to become directly involved in creating positive change on campus.

All undergraduate students are welcome to attend, share concerns, propose ideas, and get involved in University Affairs initiatives.

events.description:

This event is co-hosted with the International Student Success Office.

events.title: Bioethics Society GBM #5
events.description:
Join the Bioethics Society for a fun and competitive Bioethics Jeopardy GBM! Students will split into teams and test their knowledge across different bioethics-related categories, which may include medical ethics, famous cases, healthcare dilemmas, genetics, public health, technology, and general science trivia.

Questions will range from easier introductory topics to more challenging scenarios, so no prior bioethics experience is required. Teams will work together to choose categories, answer questions, earn points, and compete for prizes at the end of the game. 

This GBM is a great way to learn about important bioethical topics in a more interactive format while meeting other students and putting your teamwork and trivia skills to the test!

events.description:

This experience provides a valuable opportunity where students will be able to view real anatomical structures and gain insight into an important aspect of physical therapy education. 

**Important:** Students must have attended **at least 2 previous Pre-PT Club meetings** in order to be eligible to attend this event. Please make sure you meet this requirement before signing up.

USG and Student Engagement & Activities invite club leaders to the Club Co-Lab Series, a set of collaborative working sessions organized by club category. Each Co-Lab is designed to help organizations meet relevant partners, share resources, develop joint-event ideas, and leave with practical next steps for collaboration.

Each session will include networking, an icebreaker, a brief USG presentation on funding, treasury information, the Club Closet, and important SEA guidelines, followed by a department-specific resource presentation and interactive collaboration activities. Clubs will take part in activities such as Resources Bingo, scenario planning, and a “Build Your Own Event” challenge that helps them identify potential partners and turn an idea into a feasible program.

USG will also collect feedback and follow up on collaboration commitments so that these conversations lead to real partnerships, shared programming, and stronger support for clubs throughout the year. Attendees will have the opportunity to win snacks and gift-card incentives.

We strongly encourage each organization to send at least two representatives, ideally members of the club’s Core Four: President, Vice President, Secretary, and Treasurer.

events.title: The Beer Goggles Challenge
events.description:
The Beer Goggles Challenge is an activity designed to simulate the effects of alcohol impairment. Participants wear specially designed goggles that distort vision and coordination, mimicking the sensation of being intoxicated. During the challenge, students attempt simple tasks like walking in a straight line, picking up objects, or navigating obstacles. The goal is to demonstrate how alcohol impairs judgment, reaction time, and motor skills, reinforcing the dangers of driving under the influence or engaging in risky behaviors while intoxicated. It provides a hands-on, impactful learning experience about the real-world consequences of alcohol impairment.
